guides.title: Collect delivery metrics from GitHub and Jira
Run an internal AI readiness assessment
Create a use-case and ROI tracker

install.claude: claude mcp add --scope project tenhaw -- npx -y @tenhaw/mcp@1.1.0

tools.title: AI readiness assessment
tools.use: Assess organisational AI readiness from evidence-backed answers across six dimensions.
tools.method: Thirty anchored questions. Dimension means are combined using explicit weights and renormalised over answered dimensions. Response coverage is reported separately; bands are withheld below 80% coverage. Empty responses produce an unavailable score. This is self-assessment support, not certification or legal advice.
tools.snippet:
import { scoreReadiness } from '@tenhaw/ai-readiness';
console.log(scoreReadiness({ answers: [{ questionId: 'strategy-1', score: 3 }] }));

tools.title: Delivery metrics
tools.use: Calculate five DORA metrics and flow observations for one service from linked delivery events.
tools.method: Observed production deployments, linked commits and incidents underpin five DORA metrics. Tags and merges are excluded as deployment proxies. Missing evidence remains unavailable. Periods are half-open [since, until), timestamps require timezones, and services are computed separately. Health output is informational, with data improvement prompts and no invented composite ranking.

tools.title: AI ROI and project cost
tools.use: Compare low, base and high AI business-case assumptions without treating recovered staff capacity as cash by default.
tools.method: Monthly cash flows include adoption, explicit cash realisation, build cost, ongoing cost and discounting. Cash realisation defaults to zero in examples. Capacity hours remain separate. NPV discounts monthly flows by (1 + annual rate)^(month / 12). Payback is null if cumulative cash flow never breaks even. All cost defaults are editable assumptions, not quotes or financial advice.

tools.title: AI use-case register
tools.use: Keep use-case ownership, value, feasibility and governance review together in a structured register.
tools.method: Priority is value multiplied by feasibility, each between 0 and 5. Prohibited indicative uses are blocked; high or unknown risk requires review. Governance gates precede score ordering. Risk descriptions are indicative, not legal advice. Transparency obligations may coexist with high-risk obligations.

tools.title: Product operating model
tools.api: generateOperatingModel({ teams, okrs, roadmap, interactions }); renderMermaid(report)
tools.use: Validate team ownership, outcome-led roadmaps, OKRs and team interactions.
tools.method: Team types and interactions reference Team Topologies without affiliation. Checks identify missing ownership, outcomes and support declarations. They prompt design conversations rather than prescribe an organisation. Key-result progress is (current - baseline) / (target - baseline), supporting decreasing targets.

agentSetup.secretHandling: Local environment only. Report missing variable names; never copy values into commands, configuration or logs.
agentSetup.onePrompt: Install Tenhaw Kit {version} for this project and continue my requested task. Identify the coding client and project directory, then run npx -y tenhaw@{version} setup --agent CLIENT --directory PROJECT --json using the detected client and project path in place of CLIENT and PROJECT. Inspect the plan, preserve existing servers and instructions, and report conflicting Tenhaw definitions for review. Apply the configuration with the same command plus --yes --verify. Verify the expected eight local tools and a synthetic readiness calculation. If I request a starter, scaffold a new directory, install its dependencies and run its documented build and tests. Ask me to set only missing local environment variables required for GitHub or Jira collection I request. Keep secret values out of chat, command arguments, configuration and logs. Report the checks that passed and any remaining host reload, enablement or trust step; confirm a tool call inside the coding client after that step.
